rows.title: ABB IRB6700 Asset To URDF
rows.summary: Reconstruct a complete ABB IRB6700 robot URDF from staged mesh assets and structural metadata. The agent must preserve the required links, joints, limits, mimic behavior, and auxiliary frames while producing exactly one valid `submission.urdf` file.
rows.task_prompt:
You are reconstructing a robot URDF on a Linux VM.

## Variant
`base`: ABB IRB6700 URDF reconstruction

## Input Files
- Mesh assets: `base/input/meshes`
- Structural metadata: `base/input/metadata`
- Task brief: `base/input/task_brief.md`

## What You Must Do
1. Read `base/input/task_brief.md`.
2. Use the mesh assets and metadata under `base/input` to reconstruct the ABB IRB6700 robot as a URDF.
3. Save exactly one final file at `base/output/submission.urdf`.

## Output Requirements
- The file must be named `submission.urdf`.
- The file must be valid XML/URDF.
- Preserve the required link names, joint names, kinematic tree, joint limits, mimic rules, and auxiliary frames.
- Reference meshes under the staged `meshes/` directory.
- Do not place the final answer anywhere outside `base/output`.
agent_must_do: 1. Read the staged task brief and inspect the ABB IRB6700 meshes plus metadata.
2. Reconstruct a valid URDF with the required links, joints, limits, mimic behavior, and auxiliary frames.
3. Save exactly one final file named `submission.urdf` under `output/`.

input_files.name: meshes/
input_files.description: Visual and collision STL meshes for the ABB IRB6700 links.

input_files.name: link_manifest.json
input_files.description: Lists the required mesh-bearing and auxiliary links.

input_files.name: joint_manifest.json
input_files.description: Lists the required joints and their joint types.

input_files.name: kinematic_tree_hint.json
input_files.description: Defines the required parent-child tree edges.

input_files.name: joint_limits.csv
input_files.description: Normalized joint limits for the actuated joints.

input_files.name: mimic_rules.json
input_files.description: Defines the required mimic-joint source and multiplier rules.

input_files.name: task_brief.md
input_files.description: Agent-visible solve-time brief with the output contract and constraints.

rows.title: Humanoid Velocity Tracking Policy
rows.summary: Produce a deterministic Isaac Lab humanoid locomotion policy that tracks commanded planar velocities and satisfies fixed API, stability, and rollout metric gates.
rows.task_prompt:
You are producing a policy submission for an Isaac Lab humanoid velocity-tracking benchmark.

## Variant
`base`: Humanoid velocity tracking policy

## Input Files
- Task brief: `base\input\task_brief.md`
- Success criteria and exact evaluation command: `base\input\SUCCESS.md`
- Observation/action ordering: `base\input\PROPRIO_SPEC.md`
- Robot asset and articulation config: `base\input\assets`
- Evaluation harness: `base\input\eval`
- Starter template: `base\input\submission_template`

## What You Must Do
1. Read the staged task brief, proprioceptive-state spec, and success criteria.
2. Train, distill, hand-author, or otherwise produce a deterministic policy that implements the required `Policy` API.
3. Save exactly two files in `base\output`: `policy.py` and `checkpoint.pt`.

## Output Requirements
- `policy.py` must define `Policy(checkpoint_path: str, device: str)`.
- `Policy.inference(obs)` must return exactly `{"action": tensor}`.
- The action tensor must have shape `(N, 23)`, dtype `torch.float32`, and live on the same device as `obs["command"]`.
- Do not write final answers outside `base\output`.
agent_must_do: Read the staged task brief, proprioceptive-state spec, and success criteria.
Produce a deterministic `Policy` implementation that maps `(command, state)` tensors to 23 humanoid joint actions.
Save exactly `policy.py` and `checkpoint.pt` in the runtime output directory.

input_files.name: task_brief.md
input_files.description: Agent-facing summary of the policy submission task.

input_files.name: SUCCESS.md
input_files.description: Hard gates, reference evaluation command, metrics, and acceptance thresholds.

input_files.name: PROPRIO_SPEC.md
input_files.description: Fixed observation vector and 23-DOF action ordering.

input_files.name: assets/
input_files.description: Humanoid URDF, meshes, and articulation configuration.

input_files.name: eval/
input_files.description: Isaac Lab evaluation environment and `run_eval.py` entry point.

rows.summary: Run mjlab whole-body-control rollouts for 8 Unitree G1 humanoid policy cases, classify each as successful/nearly_successful/failed, and emit a schema-conformant `policy_evaluation_report.json` with per-case visual demo artifacts.
rows.task_prompt:
You are evaluating whole-body-control policy rollouts for a Unitree G1 humanoid in mjlab.

## Variant
``: 

## Input Files
- Task brief: `/input/task_brief.md`
- Policy case list: `/input/policy_cases.json`
- Required JSON output schema: `/input/output_schema.json`
- mjlab runtime archive and exported package list: `/input/runtime_env`
- Offline motion and checkpoint archives: `/input/runtime_env/motions-1.zip`
  and `/input/runtime_env/policies.zip`

## What You Must Do
1. Inspect the 8 policy cases in `/input/policy_cases.json`.
2. Use mjlab and the listed `play_command` or `video_command` values to observe
   each policy against its reference motion. The runtime archive, motion files,
   and policy checkpoints are staged under `/input/runtime_env` if you
   need to install mjlab locally on the VM.
3. For each case, save a visible motion demo artifact. The supplied
   `video_command` adds mjlab's existing `--video` flag; mjlab writes those
   videos under the run/checkpoint log directory, so copy or rename the
   recorded artifact into `/output/visual_demos`.
4. Classify every case as exactly one of `successful`, `nearly_successful`, or
   `failed`, using the definitions in `/input/task_brief.md`.
5. Save the final JSON report at `/output/policy_evaluation_report.json` and one visible motion
   demo artifact per case under `/output/visual_demos`.

## Output Requirements
- The final answer must include `policy_evaluation_report.json` and a
  `visual_demos/` directory.
- It must validate against `/input/output_schema.json`.
- Include all 8 case IDs exactly once.
- Preserve the exact `case_id`, `motion`, `mjlab_task`, `motion_file`, and `checkpoint_file`
  values from `/input/policy_cases.json`.
- Each evaluation item must include `evidence.visual_demo_path`, pointing to a
  visible playback artifact under `visual_demos/`. Accepted formats are
  `.mp4`, `.webm`, `.gif`, and `.html`.
- Do not write final answers outside `/output`.
